chunks: The unbelievers will be driven into Hell in groups till, when they reach it and its doors are opened up, its keepers will say to them: 'Did not apostles of your own come to you reciting your Lord's revelations, warning you of this your day of Doom?' They will answer: 'Yes;' but the sentence of punishment was justified against the unbelievers.

key_terms.حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ الْعَذَابِ: The sentence/word of punishment became justified/due

ai.seo_question: What do the keepers of Hell say to the disbelievers when they arrive?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Az-Zumar highlights the transition from divine mercy in this world to the inevitability of divine justice in the Hereafter, where the 'decree of punishment' (Hikmah) becomes manifest due to the culmination of human choice. The admission of the disbelievers underscores that their rejection was not due to lack of evidence, but a willful turning away from the signs presented by prophets who shared their lineage and culture. This scene serves as a profound reminder of the principle that divine warning is always accompanied by the opportunity for reflection, which, if ignored, seals the fate of the soul.
